drift_findings.rationale: The implementation satisfies the approved upstream's pinned interfaces and success criteria, with three non-substantive scope divergences, all disclosed. (1) Section 5.1's required correction of the parent design's commit sketch from singular path to plural paths was not made because the committed parent design already sketches the plural form — the approved claim's intent is already true, so no governing document is left inaccurate. (2) The delivered file scope exceeds Section 5.1's enumeration by two source fixes (shared fixed-point gate composition and the archive supersession predicate split) plus a commit-authorization path-ordering contract correction in src/contracts/gates.ts; the first two fall under Section 4.6's explicit allowance for fence/ownership corrections the journeys expose, and the third is a pre-existing latent defect that blocked Section 4.5's own commit-authorization gate from opening on its composed context. All three are recorded as deviations in phases/3/impl-notes.md with regression tests. (3) docs/PATTERNS.md, listed in Section 5.3's maintained-page set, was not updated; inspection of that page shows it carries no implementation-workflow claim that Phase 3 changed (only file-naming conventions and fixture counts), so no maintained claim is stale. None of these alters the approved ownership boundary, the two distinct human boundaries, the client-owned Git rule, or the phase's declared exclusions of Phase 4 work.

rule_findings.rationale: Every deliverable maps to the approved phase design's pinned interfaces: plural commit.paths (src/contracts/semantic-workflow.ts:109-115) per Section 4.2, the enabled phase-impl invocation and commit-facts projection with blocked/inspect fallback (src/state/semantic-view.ts:286-299) per Section 4.2/5.1, both-direction submission validation before composition (src/state/semantic-actions.ts:89-115, 387) per Section 4.3, and the skill rewrite per Section 4.7. The two source fixes beyond the enumerated list (shared fixed-point gate composition in src/state/request-composition.ts:569-609 and the archive supersession predicate split in src/state/semantic-status.ts:251-271) fall inside Section 4.6's explicit allowance for fence/ownership corrections the journeys expose, and both are recorded as deviations in phases/3/impl-notes.md. The design's one required parent-design correction was verified unnecessary (the committed parent design already sketches plural paths) and that is recorded rather than silently dropped. The gates.ts commit-authorization ordering correction is a latent pre-existing contract defect blocking the design's own success criterion, disclosed in the notes with both-direction tests. No governing document is left contradicting shipped behavior: the notes, LIMITATIONS.md, OVERVIEW.md, and the maintained pages were updated in the same change.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: The subject is a phase-3 implementation output produced at phase-impl-3 under the approved phase design (phases/3/design.md, content digest 6fc848793c09...) listed as a parent document, and it changes source, contracts, skills, tests, and docs.

rule_findings.rationale: Commit facts are projected only from authenticated commit-authorization authority; missing facts map to blocked/inspect with no invented values (src/state/semantic-view.ts:286-289), and commit remains non-offerable (canOffer excludes "commit", src/state/semantic-view.ts:369-371), so no apply call can manufacture commit authority. Implementation commits carry requires_human_confirmation: true while design milestones carry false, keeping the durable authorization and the conversational commit confirmation distinct. The rewritten skill (skills/archflow-phase-impl/SKILL.md:42-44) requires stopping for explicit human judgment, forbids choosing or inferring a decision, treats waiver-requested and cancellation as non-approval, and requires showing the staged diff and exact message for explicit confirmation with "no prior conversation substitutes for it". Decisions are submitted only as an opaque server-issued option token plus the human's reason; agent prose and elapsed time confer nothing. Under tool unavailability the skill mandates stopping with no staging, commit, or offline authorization record.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: The change opens the commit-authorization human gate on the semantic surface and projects implementation commit facts with requires_human_confirmation, and rewrites the skill that presents human decisions.

rule_findings.rationale: Failure states remain visible non-success with a safe next action: submission-shape mismatches now return SEMANTIC_SUBMISSION_MISMATCH with the fresh safe view instead of an unhandled composer TypeError (src/state/semantic-actions.ts:94-115), a composer/status disagreement refuses composition as transitionInvalid("gate-fixed-point-disagreement") rather than composing an unadvertised gate (src/state/request-composition.ts:595-597), and unauthenticated archives, missing presentations, and unavailable commit authority all project blocked/inspect (src/state/semantic-view.ts:149-154, 211, 257, 266, 288). The discovered one-hop simple-revision wedge is reported honestly rather than hidden: docs/LIMITATIONS.md:81-87 records the unsupported case, its mitigation, and why it is accepted, the impl notes name the exact TRANSITION_INVALID edge, and the regression journey stops at that boundary. Verification evidence is reported faithfully, including the two release-offline failures before regeneration and the final green re-run against post-remediation bytes.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: The change adds failure and blocked paths (submission mismatch, gate-fixed-point disagreement, unavailable commit authority) and reports a discovered unfixed defect.

rule_findings.rationale: The relaxation is narrowly scoped and still fails closed. archiveAuthenticates keeps full validateDurableSemantics cross-binding of the request/decision pair, and archiveBinds additionally requires the archive's task_id and phase_instance to equal the current state's; unreadable or cross-binding-invalid archives keep the conservative invalid classification (src/state/semantic-status.ts:261-264), while only a semantically valid pair that no longer binds the current position yields an empty enrichment — conferring no waiver origin, no revision checkpoint, and therefore no advancement authority. The open-gate branch still pins gate_id, kind, subject_digest, context_digest, and opened_at_revision before treating an archive as exact. Semantic status refuses to project when durable state's repository_identity_digest differs from the transaction authority, and offers bind repository identity, task, revision, and input fingerprint, so cross-repository or cross-task reuse cannot authorize an action. The gates.ts change only aligns the authorized-path ordering rule with the code-unit ordering used everywhere else; it still requires a sorted, duplicate-free, non-empty path set bound to the subject's diff and artifact digests.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: The change alters how archived gate requests/decisions are classified as authority (src/state/semantic-status.ts:133-149, 251-271) and how commit/gate context bytes are validated (src/contracts/gates.ts:159-172).
